rooms.question: Can a path remember which way to grow when no individual holds the whole network?
rooms.ontology: An agent is a moving state; a field stores numbers over cells. Here deposited trail changes what later agents sense: environmental memory.
rooms.action: Watch a bright connection and keep it in view when the anchor arrangement changes automatically; wait at least one 20-second transition.
rooms.observable: The caption cycles triad, ring, pair, scattered; trail concentrations change and fade rather than being one pre-drawn network.
rooms.mechanism: 300 agents in the scene sense left/centre/right, turn and deposit. PhysarumGrid multiplies concentration by .95 and mixes four neighbours with .5 diffusion. Fixed anchors also emit; their layout changes every20s.
rooms.limit: A simulated trail is not proof of a shortest route or a biological nervous system. Chosen anchors and boundary conditions determine which networks can appear.
rooms.variation: Existing passive variation: compare two automatic anchor layouts. Proposed: visitor-grabbable anchors or a pause control; neither is currently exposed.
rooms.prior_bridge: Earlier emergent patterns arose from many updates; now the environment retains those updates.
rooms.next_bridge: The next room supplies a field from outside instead of letting agents write it.

rooms.question: If many agents turn together, must they be watching one another?
rooms.ontology: A vector field assigns a direction to a position; an integration field records costs to a target. An agent can navigate by reading its local direction.
rooms.action: Follow one arrow and one agent through the automatic tour: open field, block, U-wall, zigzag, wind, noise.
rooms.observable: Obstacles reorganize the arrow pattern; wind has a direction without a destination. The tour advances every10s and remains in noise at the end.
rooms.mechanism: A40×40 cost grid is propagated from a target, then vectors point toward lower costs.200agents steer toward their current cell vector; near zero vectors they wander.
rooms.limit: Common motion can come from shared infrastructure rather than agreement. Cost maps choose what counts as a traversable route.
rooms.variation: Existing comparison: observe the tour. Proposed: hide arrows while holding a scenario fixed using curator scenario/field_display configuration; visitor VR wall placement is not implemented.
rooms.prior_bridge: Physarum writes its own field; this field is provided to the agents.
rooms.next_bridge: Boids instead compute directions from neighbouring agents.

rooms.question: Which local relationship is making this flock hold together?
rooms.ontology: Separation, alignment and cohesion are distinct steering contributions; weights determine their relative influence on an agent velocity.
rooms.action: Follow the highlighted boid and its coloured force arrows. Change one SEP, ALIGN or COH slider while leaving the other settings alone.
rooms.observable: The highlighted agent exposes red separation, blue alignment and green cohesion; population motion changes as one contribution gains weight.
rooms.mechanism: Each update gathers neighbours within a perception radius, averages headings/positions, and sums weighted forces. Positions wrap around the displayed bounds.
rooms.limit: A flock pattern cannot establish consent or a universal ideal balance. The boundary wraps and the neighbour radius already decide who is in relation.
rooms.variation: Existing: alter perception RADIUS, then see whether the same rule weights still make the same group. Proposed: asymmetric perception to test whose movements become visible.
rooms.prior_bridge: The flow field supplied common direction; here neighbours supply it.
rooms.next_bridge: Agent-based modelling generalizes from these three rules to state and environment.

rooms.question: How much of a collective result changes when one rule changes?
rooms.ontology: An agent-based model stores individual states and update rules; population outcomes are produced by repeated interaction with shared state.
rooms.action: Watch the colony, raise EVAPORATE, and compare trail persistence; use RESET before a second comparison. MODE cycles the displayed behavioural mode.
rooms.observable: The trail heatmap loses or retains marks at different rates. ANTS changes population between5and80 and respawns the agents.
rooms.mechanism: Agents sense/deposit a pheromone grid, consume food and switch behaviours; evaporation is a shared field update. MODE selects three model modes; this is one model family, not arbitrary rule programming.
rooms.limit: An aggregate picture does not validate the agents as models of people. What agents can sense and what the shared grid remembers are design choices.
rooms.variation: Existing: compare many short-lived traces with fewer lasting traces using ANTS and EVAPORATE separately. Proposed: agents with differing sensor capacities.
rooms.prior_bridge: Boids used three steering terms; now rules include internal state and a lasting environment.
rooms.next_bridge: The next room concentrates on two trail types and the journey between home and food.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Other placed catalyst hazards may disturb observation; no safe/quiet museum encounter verified. Old intent describes physical platforms constraining agents, not confirmed by selected internal2Dmodel.

rooms.question: How can an ant leave useful directions without carrying a map?
rooms.ontology: Stigmergy coordinates activity through a shared medium. This colony uses two numerical trail channels: home and food.
rooms.action: Observe ants leaving the centre and returning from either food anchor. Compare fresh bright trails with areas no longer visited.
rooms.observable: Ants change direction/state on reaching food or home, with trail information persisting in the ground between visits.
rooms.mechanism: FORAGING ants seek food channel and deposit home channel; RETURNING ants reverse that relation. Three local sensors steer movement; trail energy decays until reset at a destination.
rooms.limit: This scene is a spatial foraging model, not a demonstrated travelling-salesman solver. Efficient-looking trails alone do not prove global optimality.
rooms.variation: Existing: compare the two fixed food directions. Proposed: curator anchorage ring/triad/scattered variants or movablefood; there is no visitor food-layout control in this scene.
rooms.prior_bridge: Agent-based modelling exposed rules; here external memory makes one specific rule family legible.
rooms.next_bridge: Particle swarms move that memory into personal and shared best positions.

rooms.question: When a swarm improves, who decided what better means?
rooms.ontology: A particle keeps its own best position and follows a swarm best; fitness is the scoring rule that names these positions best.
rooms.action: Watch CONVERGE, then press SPREAD, then NOVELTY. Keep INERTIA fixed during the comparison.
rooms.observable: The same kind of moving population collects toward the centre, favours distance from it, or seeks distance from archived positions according to the chosen score.
rooms.mechanism: Velocity combines inertia, personal-best displacement and global-best displacement with randomweights. CONVERGE rewards negative radius; SPREAD positive radius; NOVELTY distance to the nearest archived position.
rooms.limit: Optimization inherits its purpose from the objective; a high score cannot establish that a social outcome is desirable. Novelty also depends on what the archive remembers.
rooms.variation: Existing: choose novelty as the primary aim instead of treating dispersal as failure; then vary INERTIA. Proposed: compare two explicit conflicting objectives simultaneously.
rooms.prior_bridge: Ants store traces in the environment; particles retain best positions.
rooms.next_bridge: The capstone asks which less visible rules keep a collective system going.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

rooms.question: If this small ecosystem persists, which rules are helping it persist?
rooms.ontology: A population is coupled to resources, predation and reproduction. A simulation may include a separate stabilizer as well as individual agent rules.
rooms.action: Read the Prey, Pred and Food counts, then track a food loss or population change before returning to the counts.
rooms.observable: Population and food counts change; prey seek food/flee predators and predators seek prey. The simulation also restocks agents under explicit thresholds.
rooms.mechanism: Food renews, parents exchange/mutate numericDNA, and balance_ecosystem adds5prey below10, weakens predators above halfprey, and may restock2predators. Default quota is tended.
rooms.limit: Persistence is not evidence of self-regulation alone: a coded referee assists it. This room contains one ecosystem artifact, not the multi-algorithm showcase imagined in old intent.
rooms.variation: Existing: distinguish agent events from count changes plausibly due to restocking. Proposed: compare curator quota fallow/barren/hunted configurations or expose restocking as a visitor control.
rooms.prior_bridge: After changing the PSO objective, look for the less visible objective embodied in population maintenance.
rooms.next_bridge: Machine learning next makes adjustment and evaluation explicit.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Do not claim no referee, natural equilibrium or implemented swarm-algorithm switcher.
